facts: Assume a Max Bögl entity manufactures its own new precast concrete structural elements in Germany and first supplies them commercially in Germany for permanent incorporation into construction works.

The supplied product is a finished structural element. The scenario does not cover reused products, lifts, escalators, components sold separately, drinking-water contact products, or sales in outermost EU regions.
No specific harmonised specification, product-family transition date, or conformity assessment file has been supplied.
Assume a Max Bögl entity operates an asphalt plant in Germany and operates its separate 8 MW rated thermal input natural-gas boiler for heat.
Assume the boiler began operation in 2017 and is used regularly. The boiler is neither an engine nor a gas turbine. Its combustion gases are not used directly to heat or dry materials.
No operating permit, national implementing text, or evidence of an exemption has been supplied.
Assume a Max Bögl entity buys cement for its German precast concrete production from an independent German supplier that manufactures that cement in a clinker kiln.
Assume the Max Bögl entity neither operates the supplier's kiln nor manufactures cement, lime or magnesium oxide in this scenario. It depends on this supplier for the specified cement input.
No supplier permit, plant configuration beyond the clinker kiln, or evidence about cost, contract or availability effects has been supplied.
